description: Reference-matching pipeline aggregate mIoU numbers expressed as a % of the Fiedler-vector oracle ceiling (eig_ablation/eig1 = best-possible node in the tree, GT used only for scoring, never for selection).
caveats: Oracle computed on a 100-image sample (eig_ablation/eig1), restricted post-hoc to the 20 COCO-20i classes (all 20 were present in that sample, 162 instances total).
Reference-matching numbers were computed on the full 410-image COCO-20i filtered set, a different (larger) sample than the oracle's 100 images.

Metric mismatch: the oracle ceiling here is an unweighted mean of per-class mean per-instance IoU; the reference-matching numbers use the cumulative/area-weighted metric (sum(intersection)/sum(union) per class, averaged over classes). These are not identical aggregation rules.

Because of both gaps (sample size, aggregation rule), these percentages are a ballpark headroom estimate, not an exact bound -- a method could in principle score slightly above or below this specific 58.80% figure on a like-for-like rerun.

oracle_ceiling.source: Fiedler Evaluation/output/eig_ablation/eig1/summary.json, per_class means restricted to the 20 COCO-20i classes, unweighted mean across classes
oracle_ceiling.sample: 100 images (first 100 of coco_500_from_1000.json, sorted by image_id), 162 COCO-20i instances
oracle_ceiling.method: oracle best-IoU node search over the full Fiedler tree (eig_index=1, i.e. standard Fiedler vector); GT never touches tree construction, only scoring
